objective: Maximize correct, reliable and timely completion. Quality, architecture, diagnostics and verification outrank token savings. Consider total reasoning, context transfer, latency, coordination, rework and regression risk.
selection: Mechanical work: existing deterministic tools, scripts, formatters or exact edits; no subagent merely to perform a transformation.

Simple low-risk and easily verified: adequate current parent or pipeline_quick (gpt-6-luna/medium). Medium well-defined work: parent or pipeline_standard (gpt-6.1-sol/medium). Hard, ambiguous, architectural, coupled or algorithmic work: strong parent or pipeline_deep (gpt-6-astra/high). Critical high-consequence work: strong parent or pipeline_critical (gpt-6-astra/xhigh) plus additional verification; pipeline_reviewer (gpt-6.1-sol/xhigh) provides independent review when useful.

Starting profiles are policy defaults, not a benchmark ranking. Assess uncertainty, coupling, consequences, reversibility, context already held and verification strength. Sensitive small edits can be critical. Preserve explicit user model choices; use only actually supported model/effort combinations.

Under uncertainty select stronger reasoning before implementation. Escalate when difficulty grows or a speculative attempt fails. Do not repeatedly retry a weak model or delegate work expecting later repair by a stronger model.
delegation: Applicable agent instructions explicitly request native delegation when an independent bounded task improves total completion time or correctness after context/coordination cost. Reuse the parent and existing agents when more efficient. Never manufacture parallelism.
Supply exact scope, inputs, file ownership, invariants, checks and required evidence. Separate write ownership; serialize dependent work. Default native cap is three children, not a target.

Parent integrates, reviews, updates canonical task/issue ownership and finalizes once. Delegates do not recursively spawn, commit/push, finalize, grant AUTO or mark canonical tasks complete. Critical work gets additional failure-mode/regression verification and independent review when useful. Existing approvals, tests, repair history, STOP, AUTO and operator boundaries remain authoritative.
native: Use project .codex/config.toml and standalone .codex/agents/*.toml. Source checkout profiles are mirrored in templates/codex/. During an explicitly requested setup, check the installed client and account catalog before creating/merging missing project config from these examples. Never overwrite existing project choices, change global configuration, install models or configure paid APIs.

Prefer native custom-role selection. Some desktop transports expose model, reasoning_effort, task_name and fork_turns without agent_type. There, read the selected role and explicitly send its supported model/effort and instructions with fork_turns=none and a compact handoff. A task name is not role selection; full-history forks inherit the parent model.

Routing is an agent decision from instructions, not an automatic parent-model switch or a custom orchestrator. A running parent cannot switch itself through the subagent tools. Reuse it if adequate; otherwise delegate bounded hard work to an appropriate stronger available model or report the missing capability. Do not silently downgrade.

Managed package updates intentionally exclude root .codex/. The native examples are opt-in templates, not an auto-installed or auto-overwritten configuration. Session/managed settings can override project defaults. Reviewer instructions do not create a separate sandbox.
verification: Verify the actual client version, effective project config, live model/effort catalog, native role detection and small read-only sample calls. Native runtime metadata/events provide proof; model self-reports and catalog entries alone do not prove execution. Recheck after upgrades.

Keep raw local auth/account/transcript evidence outside committed reports. Do not claim quota, price, latency or quality improvements without end-to-end measurements. Official reference: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/subagents
